summary: Turn a clearance question into a solid: grow an obstacle by a moving part so the answer becomes a containment test.
objective: Build a clearance study where the obstacle is offset by the shape of the moving part, so allowed positions of that part are a visible region.
intent_signals: Show which positions of a part avoid a collision with an obstacle.
Explain how offsetting an obstacle by a part shape answers a fit question.
example_prompts: Build a Minkowski sum demonstration where I can move a part and see the forbidden region it generates.
Show the clearance envelope of a bracket around a fixed obstacle.
negative_signals: Not a general path planner: this recipe shows the region, not a route through it.
Not a tolerance analysis or manufacturing fit study.
not_for: Not a general path planner: this recipe shows the region, not a route through it.
Not a tolerance analysis or manufacturing fit study.

entities.name: Obstacle solid
entities.guidance: One fixed closed solid with clean faces; its role as the fixed operand should be stated in the scene, not inferred.

entities.name: Moving part
entities.guidance: A second solid with a marked reference point, since the sum is only meaningful relative to a declared origin on the part.

entities.name: Sum region
entities.guidance: Show the grown region as its own semi-transparent solid whose surface is generated, and mark the reference point of the part inside or outside it.

state_contract.model: Two closed solids, a declared reference point c on the moving part with local part coordinates R, and the forbidden set for that reference computed as C = O plus the set of c - r for r in R. Because the solids are closed and intersection counts as collision, C contains its boundary, so exact touching is reported as contact rather than as clearance. Membership of the reference point in C is the verdict; no contact force is computed.
state_contract.authority: The reference point position is authoritative for the verdict; the visible interpenetration of meshes is only a secondary cue and must agree with the test.
actions: Move the part and read the inside or outside verdict.
Switch the reference point to a different feature of the part.
Toggle the sum region and the original obstacle.
Reset both solids and the reference point.

invariants: The verdict is membership of the reference point in the closed forbidden region, computed with a stated predicate tolerance and never inferred from rendered overlap; boundary membership is reported as contact, a third outcome between clear and interpenetrating.
Changing the reference point changes the region: the two are one declaration and must update together.
The region always contains the obstacle itself when the part contains its own reference point.
Moving the world part moves its reference point through the forbidden region; the region itself is rebuilt only when an operand or the declared reference changes, and never translates with the part.
motion_guidance: Move the part continuously and update the verdict at every step; a verdict that only updates on release hides the boundary case.
Highlight the moment the reference point crosses the region boundary, since that is the event of interest.
known_limits: The documented convex-decomposition method splits nonconvex operands into convex pieces before combining their sums; other supported nonconvex methods may differ. Construction cost depends on the selected method and operands, with no interactive performance guarantee.
This recipe treats translation only; adding rotation changes the configuration space and is not covered here.

Boundary semantics are a declared choice: this recipe treats closed solids with touching as contact. A scene that wants touching to be legal must state open-set semantics consistently in the region, the verdict and the tolerance.
Authored guidance only: no scene runtime, rendering or numerical calibration has been run for this recipe.

claims.statement: The Minkowski sum of two point sets P and Q in d-dimensional space is the set of all sums p + q with p in P and q in Q.
claims.scope: Definition as stated in the cited documentation.

claims.statement: In motion planning the Minkowski sum of the inverted robot and the obstacles describes the positions where the robot intersects an obstacle, so its complement gives the legal positions.
claims.scope: Translation-only configuration space as described in the cited documentation.

source_refs.locator: 3D Minkowski Sum of Polyhedra, motion planning use

claims.statement: One documented approach to non-convex operands decomposes both polyhedra into convex pieces, computes all pairwise sums and merges them, with a stated worst case of order n cubed times m cubed.
claims.scope: Cost and strategy of that one documented method; other methods exist and this recipe does not claim that every non-convex algorithm requires decomposition.

source_refs.locator: 3D Minkowski Sum of Polyhedra, decomposition method and complexity

object_craft.structure: A generated solid whose surface shows the rounded and swept features that come from the part shape, not a naive uniform offset.
object_craft.material: Semi-transparent with a visible silhouette edge so the boundary can be located when the camera is inside the region.
object_craft.articulation: Rebuilt whenever either operand or the reference point changes.

object_craft.structure: A part with an obvious asymmetric feature so the shape of the grown region is clearly attributable to it.
object_craft.material: Opaque, contrasting with the region so overlap is legible; the reference point uses a dedicated marker material.
object_craft.articulation: Rigid translation only in this recipe; rotation is explicitly out of scope.

physical_contract.scope: Geometric construction and containment testing; no rigid-body dynamics or contact response.
checks: The containment verdict flips exactly when the reference point crosses the region boundary.
Rebuilding after a reference point change produces a translated region, not a different shape.
